claims.title: Forest hunter-gatherers of the Ogooué
claims.summary: Rainforest hunter-gatherers, ancestors of peoples such as the Babongo and Baka, inhabited the equatorial forest of present-day Gabon, living by hunting, fishing and gathering and trading with later farming communities.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Gabon: From the rainforest hunter-gatherers and the Bantu migrations of the Ogooué basin, through the Atlantic and slave trades of the Myènè coast, the founding of Libreville and French Equatorial Africa, to independence in 1960 and the long Bongo era ended by the coup of 2023.", terralore.co/country/GAB/chronicle#ev-3000bce-forest-hunter-gatherers-of-the-ogooue, claim TL:GAB:event:3000bce:forest-hunter-gatherers-of-the-ogooue, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Bantu farmers and ironworkers arrive
claims.summary: Bantu-speaking peoples moved into the region from the north, bringing farming, pottery and iron-working; the Ogooué valley served as a corridor of the wider Bantu expansion across Central Africa.

sources.label: Ecosystem and Relict Cultural Landscape of Lopé-Okanda

claims.title: Settlement and iron-working at Lopé-Okanda
claims.summary: The Lopé-Okanda landscape along the Ogooué preserves dense habitation sites, iron-working remains and about 1,800 rock engravings, recording the successive passage of peoples through the river corridor.

claims.title: Portuguese reach the estuary and name it Gabão
claims.summary: Portuguese navigators arrived at the estuary of the Komo River in 1472 and named it Gabão, the Portuguese word for a hooded cloak, after the estuary's shape; the country's name derives from it.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Gabon: From the rainforest hunter-gatherers and the Bantu migrations of the Ogooué basin, through the Atlantic and slave trades of the Myènè coast, the founding of Libreville and French Equatorial Africa, to independence in 1960 and the long Bongo era ended by the coup of 2023.", terralore.co/country/GAB/chronicle#ev-1472-portuguese-reach-the-estuary-and-name-it-gabao, claim TL:GAB:event:1472:portuguese-reach-the-estuary-and-name-it-gabao, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Myènè peoples settle the coast
claims.summary: Myènè-speaking peoples including the Mpongwe at the estuary, the Orungu at Cape Lopez and the Nkomi at Fernan Vaz settled the Gabon coast, organised in clans well placed to trade with the interior and the sea.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Gabon: From the rainforest hunter-gatherers and the Bantu migrations of the Ogooué basin, through the Atlantic and slave trades of the Myènè coast, the founding of Libreville and French Equatorial Africa, to independence in 1960 and the long Bongo era ended by the coup of 2023.", terralore.co/country/GAB/chronicle#ev-1100-myene-peoples-settle-the-coast, claim TL:GAB:event:1100:myene-peoples-settle-the-coast, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Peak of the Atlantic slave trade
claims.summary: The Atlantic slave trade on the Gabon coast reached its height, driven by Brazilian and Cuban demand; the Orungu kingdom and the Loango coast served as middlemen channelling captives from the interior to European slavers.

sources.label: Slave Trade of the Gabon Estuary

claims.title: Captives embarked at Gabon and Cape Lopez
claims.summary: Records describe roughly 500 captives a year being embarked at points called Gabon and Cape Lopez in the late eighteenth century, an index of the trade run through the coastal Myènè kingdoms.

sources.label: Slave Trade of the Gabon Estuary

claims.title: France treats with King Denis
claims.summary: The French officer Bouët-Willaumez signed a treaty in 1839 with the Mpongwe ruler Antchouwe Kowe Rapontchombo ("King Denis"), securing French trading and basing rights on the Gabon Estuary.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Gabon: From the rainforest hunter-gatherers and the Bantu migrations of the Ogooué basin, through the Atlantic and slave trades of the Myènè coast, the founding of Libreville and French Equatorial Africa, to independence in 1960 and the long Bongo era ended by the coup of 2023.", terralore.co/country/GAB/chronicle#ev-1839-france-treats-with-king-denis, claim TL:GAB:event:1839:france-treats-with-king-denis, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Libreville founded for freed slaves
claims.summary: Freed captives taken from a slave ship seized by the French navy were settled on the estuary in 1849; the settlement was named Libreville, "free town," and became the colonial and modern capital.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Gabon: From the rainforest hunter-gatherers and the Bantu migrations of the Ogooué basin, through the Atlantic and slave trades of the Myènè coast, the founding of Libreville and French Equatorial Africa, to independence in 1960 and the long Bongo era ended by the coup of 2023.", terralore.co/country/GAB/chronicle#ev-1849-libreville-founded-for-freed-slaves, claim TL:GAB:event:1849:libreville-founded-for-freed-slaves, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Brazza explores the Ogooué
claims.summary: Pierre Savorgnan de Brazza led expeditions up the Ogooué and on to the Congo River, founding Franceville in 1880 and signing treaties that opened the interior to French rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Gabon: From the rainforest hunter-gatherers and the Bantu migrations of the Ogooué basin, through the Atlantic and slave trades of the Myènè coast, the founding of Libreville and French Equatorial Africa, to independence in 1960 and the long Bongo era ended by the coup of 2023.", terralore.co/country/GAB/chronicle#ev-1875-brazza-explores-the-ogooue, claim TL:GAB:event:1875:brazza-explores-the-ogooue, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Gabon joins French Equatorial Africa
claims.summary: France reorganised its Central African colonies into French Equatorial Africa in 1910 — Gabon, the Middle Congo, Ubangi-Shari and Chad, governed from Brazzaville — with Gabon a separate colony.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Gabon: From the rainforest hunter-gatherers and the Bantu migrations of the Ogooué basin, through the Atlantic and slave trades of the Myènè coast, the founding of Libreville and French Equatorial Africa, to independence in 1960 and the long Bongo era ended by the coup of 2023.", terralore.co/country/GAB/chronicle#ev-1910-gabon-joins-french-equatorial-africa, claim TL:GAB:event:1910:gabon-joins-french-equatorial-africa, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Schweitzer founds the Lambaréné hospital
claims.summary: Albert Schweitzer and his wife Hélène arrived at Lambaréné on the Ogooué in 1913 and founded a hospital near a mission; it treated thousands and made Lambaréné internationally known. Schweitzer received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1952.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Gabon: From the rainforest hunter-gatherers and the Bantu migrations of the Ogooué basin, through the Atlantic and slave trades of the Myènè coast, the founding of Libreville and French Equatorial Africa, to independence in 1960 and the long Bongo era ended by the coup of 2023.", terralore.co/country/GAB/chronicle#ev-1913-schweitzer-founds-the-lambarene-hospital, claim TL:GAB:event:1913:schweitzer-founds-the-lambarene-hospital, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Overseas territory of the French Union
claims.summary: After the Second World War Gabon became an overseas territory within the French Union, gaining elected representation and laying the groundwork for African political movements led by figures such as Léon M'ba and Jean-Hilaire Aubame.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Gabon: From the rainforest hunter-gatherers and the Bantu migrations of the Ogooué basin, through the Atlantic and slave trades of the Myènè coast, the founding of Libreville and French Equatorial Africa, to independence in 1960 and the long Bongo era ended by the coup of 2023.", terralore.co/country/GAB/chronicle#ev-1946-overseas-territory-of-the-french-union, claim TL:GAB:event:1946:overseas-territory-of-the-french-union, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Oil discovered near Port-Gentil
claims.summary: Oil was discovered offshore at the Ozouri field near Port-Gentil in 1956; petroleum would become the foundation of independent Gabon's economy and a key source of state revenue.

sources.label: Gabon's Experience Managing Oil Wealth (Oil Wealth in Central Africa)

claims.title: Internal autonomy as the Gabonese Republic
claims.summary: Under the 1958 French Community Gabon became an autonomous republic with Léon M'ba as head of government, a step short of full sovereignty within the French constitutional framework.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Gabon: From the rainforest hunter-gatherers and the Bantu migrations of the Ogooué basin, through the Atlantic and slave trades of the Myènè coast, the founding of Libreville and French Equatorial Africa, to independence in 1960 and the long Bongo era ended by the coup of 2023.", terralore.co/country/GAB/chronicle#ev-1958-internal-autonomy-as-the-gabonese-republic, claim TL:GAB:event:1958:internal-autonomy-as-the-gabonese-republic, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence under Léon M'ba
claims.summary: Gabon became an independent republic on 17 August 1960, with Léon M'ba as its first leader; he was formally elected president in February 1961, maintaining close ties to France.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Gabon: From the rainforest hunter-gatherers and the Bantu migrations of the Ogooué basin, through the Atlantic and slave trades of the Myènè coast, the founding of Libreville and French Equatorial Africa, to independence in 1960 and the long Bongo era ended by the coup of 2023.", terralore.co/country/GAB/chronicle#ev-1960-independence-under-leon-m-ba, claim TL:GAB:event:1960:independence-under-leon-m-ba, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Coup attempt reversed by France
claims.summary: Military officers briefly ousted M'ba in February 1964, but French troops intervened within a day to restore him, illustrating the depth of post-independence Franco-Gabonese ties.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Gabon: From the rainforest hunter-gatherers and the Bantu migrations of the Ogooué basin, through the Atlantic and slave trades of the Myènè coast, the founding of Libreville and French Equatorial Africa, to independence in 1960 and the long Bongo era ended by the coup of 2023.", terralore.co/country/GAB/chronicle#ev-1964-coup-attempt-reversed-by-france, claim TL:GAB:event:1964:coup-attempt-reversed-by-france, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Omar Bongo takes power
claims.summary: On M'ba's death in November 1967 his vice-president Albert-Bernard (later Omar) Bongo became president; in 1968 he made the Gabonese Democratic Party the sole legal party, beginning a four-decade rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Gabon: From the rainforest hunter-gatherers and the Bantu migrations of the Ogooué basin, through the Atlantic and slave trades of the Myènè coast, the founding of Libreville and French Equatorial Africa, to independence in 1960 and the long Bongo era ended by the coup of 2023.", terralore.co/country/GAB/chronicle#ev-1967-omar-bongo-takes-power, claim TL:GAB:event:1967:omar-bongo-takes-power, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Death of Omar Bongo; Ali Bongo succeeds
claims.summary: Omar Bongo died in June 2009 after ruling for over forty years; his son Ali Bongo Ondimba won the ensuing presidential election, continuing the family's hold on power.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Gabon: From the rainforest hunter-gatherers and the Bantu migrations of the Ogooué basin, through the Atlantic and slave trades of the Myènè coast, the founding of Libreville and French Equatorial Africa, to independence in 1960 and the long Bongo era ended by the coup of 2023.", terralore.co/country/GAB/chronicle#ev-2009-death-of-omar-bongo-ali-bongo-succeeds, claim TL:GAB:event:2009:death-of-omar-bongo-ali-bongo-succeeds, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Military coup ends Bongo rule
claims.summary: After a disputed 26 August 2023 election, officers led by General Brice Oligui Nguema seized power on 30 August 2023, annulling the result and detaining Ali Bongo — ending the Bongo family's 56-year hold on the presidency.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Gabon: From the rainforest hunter-gatherers and the Bantu migrations of the Ogooué basin, through the Atlantic and slave trades of the Myènè coast, the founding of Libreville and French Equatorial Africa, to independence in 1960 and the long Bongo era ended by the coup of 2023.", terralore.co/country/GAB/chronicle#ev-2023-military-coup-ends-bongo-rule, claim TL:GAB:event:2023:military-coup-ends-bongo-rule, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
